title: Reachability Along a Chain
statement: Let $K,T$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a relation on the natural numbers, and let $c$ be a sequence of natural numbers. Define reachability at level $0$ to mean equality or one $R$-step; at each higher level, two points are reachable if there is an intermediate number less than $K$ such that each pair of successive points is reachable at the preceding level. Suppose $R(c_j,c_{j+1})$ for every $j<T$, and $c_j<K$ for every $j\le T$. Then for all natural numbers $i,j,t$ with $j+t\le T$ and $t\le 2^i$, the points $c_j$ and $c_{j+t}$ are reachable at level $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $R$ is a relation on the natural numbers
$c$ is a sequence of natural numbers
$i,j,t$ are natural numbers with $j+t\le T$ and $t\le 2^i$
